This overrides the project description's stated ~650,000 ha (§2.1.16, pp.34-35 — itself derived by excluding forest, conservancies, mining areas, urban centres and agricultural land from an initial limit of ~883,500 ha). The override is on CIP's confirmation, not on document date alone — the financial model happens to be the newer document (2026-08-13 vs 2026-03-11) and to already use 500,000 ha (Inputs, C10), but that agreement is what makes it corroborating evidence, not the reason for the override. This correction has two consequences not yet reconciled elsewhere in this file, both in financials.scenarios[0]: the ER Calculations workbook's 689,731 tCO2e/yr figure still runs on 650,647 ha, and the GIS-measured project boundary (data/geo/project_area.geojson, delegated via the geo section below) measures 652,022.0 ha — neither has been updated to reflect this confirmation. Registry status is 'under development', the status the project was submitted to the Verra registry under on 21 February 2024; it has not yet been submitted for validation. Methodology version is contested across documents: this PD applies VM0032 v1.0, while the newer project FAQ (2026-07-20) states the project will use v2.0, which was itself 'under development' at that date. An older PD (21 Feb 2024) exists and is superseded per the newest-document rule.

source_override.caveats: Read from the ER workbook rather than the financial model, which is why this figure carries its own source. This calculation runs on 650,647 ha (cell C6) — the area stated in the project description before CIP's later confirmation of 500,000 ha as the final project area (see identity.area and docs/GAPS.md, section D1). This figure has NOT been recalculated against the confirmed area: it is reported exactly as the workbook states it (Rule 3 — no interpolation, no recomputation), not adjusted to match 500,000 ha. The 3.11.26 PD (Table 1.2, p.5) states this same 689,731 figure and a 40-year total of 27,589,240 VCUs — also on the pre-confirmation area.

Three things a reader must not be left to infer. (1) The model's 500,000 ha assumption (Inputs, C10) is CIP's confirmed final project area (see identity.area) — this scenario's assumptions and outputs are correctly built on the current figure, unlike the project description and the ER Calculations workbook, which both still run on the since-superseded ~650,000 ha. (2) The $25/VCU opening price is roughly 2.7x the $9.27 average 2024 forest-carbon price in CIP's own market analysis, which is the single assumption the returns are most sensitive to. (3) The model's own investment-structure block — a named third-party investor, the invested amount, tranche percentages and the credit waterfall — is deliberately NOT reproduced in this document; see GAPS.md.

staffing_summary.text: Hiring splits in two. Professional roles — Managing Director and Deputy, Directors for Administration, Carbon, Communities, Finance and Operations, plus a Soil Scientist/Agronomist, Community Engagement Manager, Rangeland Ecologist and Quality Control/Data Manager — are recruited by the SPV drawing on CIP's, Entooma Sidai Limited's and CarbonSolve's networks in Kenya. Community roles, principally Grazing Officers and Grazing Coordinators, are selected by the participating Maasai communities themselves through their existing village structures, with elders taking the monitoring and compliance role and educated youth filling Coordinator positions. The plan states the majority of key positions and roles have already been decided, and identifies which roles are expected to be hardest to fill.

provenance.source: High-Level Staffing Plan for the Entooma Sidai Project (05-20-2026), pp.1–2
provenance.caveats: The plan names roles, not headcounts. Every employment and training headcount in the project description's own benefit-metrics table is a placeholder ('TBD', '~xx', '~xxx'), so no staffing number is stated anywhere.

ifc_ps_alignment.text: CIP maintains a standing alignment note against the IFC's eight Performance Standards on Environmental and Social Sustainability (2012): assessment and management of E&S risks; labour and working conditions; resource efficiency and pollution prevention; community health, safety and security; land acquisition and involuntary resettlement; biodiversity conservation; Indigenous Peoples; and cultural heritage. The note walks each standard and states which project procedure addresses it.

provenance.source: Climate Investment Partners' Alignment with the International Finance Corporation's Performance Standards (5-21-2026)
provenance.caveats: A self-assessment by the developer, not an external audit finding or an IFC determination.

items.question: What prevents this project running into the controversies reported between Maasai communities and other carbon projects?
items.answer: The FAQ's answer rests on four structural differences from the Northern Kenya Grassland Carbon Project (Verra ID 1468): the project was initiated by the local Maasai communities themselves rather than introduced to them; the project area is ethnically homogenous, so the interethnic conflicts seen elsewhere are not expected; it operates on privately-owned land rather than community land, so each individual landowner undergoes FPIC and signs up individually; and grazing plans are developed by the communities' own elders rather than imposed. The answer is a design argument, not an outcome yet observed.

provenance.source: FAQs for Entooma Sidai Project (7-20-2026), Q4

items.question: How much land is signed up, and how binding is it?
items.answer: 315,000+ hectares are signed under Letters of Intent against a target of 500,000 to 650,000 hectares. LOIs are not the binding instrument: the project intends to engage one of two Kenyan law firms to run land-title searches against the national registry and draft the Benefit Sharing Agreement that transfers carbon rights. Neither the firm engagement nor those agreements had happened as at the FAQ's date.

provenance.source: FAQs for Entooma Sidai Project (7-20-2026), Q7

items.question: Has the Kenyan government's revenue share been agreed?
items.answer: No. The project states it will follow all fees set out in the Climate Change (Carbon Markets) Regulations, 2024, but the exact amount remains to be determined, with discussions ongoing with both Narok County officials and NEMA as Kenya's national focal point.

provenance.source: FAQs for Entooma Sidai Project (7-20-2026), Q10

items.question: Which version of the VM0032 methodology will the project use?
items.answer: The FAQ states the project will use the latest version of VM0032 — version 2.0, which was itself 'under development' as of 20 July 2026 — and expects only a negligible effect on emission reductions, with the project likely to issue removals only. The project description on file applies v1.0, so the two documents differ on this point.

provenance.source: FAQs for Entooma Sidai Project (7-20-2026), Q9; version applied per Entooma Sidai CCB-and-VCS Project Description, 3.11.26, p.9
provenance.caveats: Included because it is a live methodology risk: a project cannot validate against a methodology version that is still under development, and the newer of the two documents is the one asserting the newer version.
